jobs.description: The University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein (UKSH) combines world-class international research with interdisciplinary patient care. We are the state's only comprehensive care provider and its largest employer. Our approximately 17,500 employees ensure highly personalized care—which is indispensable for the people of Schleswig-Holstein.The University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein (UKSH) with its locations in Kiel and Lübeck is one of the largest medical care centers in Europe. It serves to warrant maximum medical care in the northernmost federal state and guarantees medical-technical care at the highest level, especially for patients who require highly differentiated diagnosis and therapy. The unique feature of university medicine is the interaction of health care, research and teaching with the result that scientific findings flow directly into the health system.Our research aims to develop novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for chronic inflammatory diseases, including inflammatory bowel, liver, lung and skin diseases. To achieve this, we investigate the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying immune regulation in different disease contexts and employ state-of-the-art technologies to comprehensively characterize human immune cells, with a particular focus on antigen-specific CD4+ T cells. A major focus of our research is the integration of high-dimensional single-cell and immune repertoire data. Your work will focus on the computational analysis, integration and interpretation of high-dimensional sequencing data, with particular emphasis on:- Analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing, T cell receptor sequencing, and ATAC sequencing data- Integration of transcriptomic, TCR, epigenetic and flow cytometry data to characterize immune cell states and regulatory mechanisms- Development and application of reproducible bioinformatics workflows and analysis pipelines, including data visualization and interpretation- Active contribution to diverse collaborative projects within the group, including the planning and design of computational analyses in close interaction with experimental scientistsStart in our team:Join our research team starting from February 1st 2027. The position is initially limited to two years, with the possibility of extension. part-time employment may be compatible within the framework of certain working time models- Exceptional technical infrastructure especially for multi-dimensional flow-cytometry and for next generation sequencing at the the Institute of Medical Immunology and the Center of Molecular Biosciences (ZMB)- You can find more exciting benefits offered by the UKSH here:Benefits (uksh.de)What you can expect:- A fascinating research environment for the investigation of basic processes of human immune reactions with direct implications for immune-mediated diseases- A systematic training to work independently in a challenging and diversified research field- The opportunity to work in a dedicated, supportive and international research team- An extensive pool of sophisticated methods and complex laboratory instrumentsWhatyou bring with you:University degree (Master's or equivalent) in bioinformatics, computational biology, biology, biostatistics, data science or a related field;
